transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, but... mostly I’m here because I’ve just been so tired lately. And it's, um, it's in a way that sleep doesn’t really seem to fix? 

I feel a little silly even bringing it up, because I know everyone gets tired, but lately even just... unloading the dishwasher, or trying to read for my certificate class, it can just feel like too much. I'm trying my best to push through it, I promise, but I just wanted to see if maybe there was something I could do better to get my energy back? Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I came in for that.
Can you tell me a bit more about how you’ve been feeling lately? Specifically, have you noticed a decrease in pleasure or interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little? I mean, I know everyone gets in a rut sometimes, right? But, um, usually I really love doing things that make me feel like myself. Like, I normally do a lot of sketching, or I go to gallery openings... and I usually love cooking, doing yoga, or even just playing tennis with a friend. 

But lately, I just... I don't know, I guess I’ve kind of stopped caring about them as much? I feel terrible even saying that out loud, because I really don't want to sound lazy or anything. I am trying to keep up with my hobbies, I promise. It's just hard to find the interest right now. Is that... is that normal when you're just feeling really run down? I hope I'm explaining that right.
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, even when you're not physically tired?

Um... I wouldn't say I feel depressed. I mean, I definitely don't want you to think I'm just sitting around moping all day. I try really hard to keep a positive attitude! 

I guess I just... I feel a little flat sometimes? Like, maybe a bit low, but I think that's mostly just because I'm so exhausted, you know? When you don't have energy, it's just hard to feel super upbeat. But I wouldn't call it depressed, really. I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been feeling a lack of energy or fatigue most days, even after resting or sleeping?

Um, yeah, I think I mentioned that earlier, actually... but, um, yes. It's just this tiredness that doesn't really go away, no matter how much I sleep. I'll wake up after a full night and still feel like I can barely manage... well, like I said, even just unloading the dishwasher or trying to focus on reading for my certificate class. It just feels like too much effort. 

I'm really sorry to repeat myself, I hope I'm not being confusing! I just... I try to rest, I really do, but the fatigue just sort of stays there. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you what you need.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating much less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Um... well, maybe just a little bit? I mean, I definitely don't want you to think I'm doing it on purpose or, like, starving myself or anything! I always try to take really good care of my health. 

But I guess my appetite has been just a little off lately. Sometimes I'll get to the end of the day and realize I’ve only really had, like, coffee and maybe a few bites of something here and there. And, um, I did notice that my jeans have gotten a little looser recently, without me actually trying to lose any weight. 

I hope that's not too concerning? I think it's mostly just because I've been so tired, you know, it's hard to muster up the energy to make a full meal. I really am trying to eat, I promise. Is that... does that make sense for what you're asking?
Have you found yourself feeling worthless or guilty, even about things that normally wouldn’t bother you?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely don't walk around feeling worthless or anything like that! I always try to see the value in myself and, you know, look on the bright side. 

I guess sometimes if I don't get everything done that I planned, like with the chores or my classwork, I might feel a tiny bit bad about it? But I think that's just normal, right? Like, anyone would feel a little guilty if they were falling behind. It's not like a deep, heavy guilt or anything. I just want to make sure I'm being a good partner and keeping up with my responsibilities. 

So, no, I wouldn't say I feel worthless at all. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to be as helpful as I can.
Have you had trouble concentrating on tasks, such as reading, following conversations, or making decisions, even when you're not physically tired?

Um, well... maybe just a little bit? I mean, I really try to stay organized, I promise. I use this planning app to keep everything on track because I want to make sure I'm staying on top of things. 

But, um... lately, I guess I have had a little trouble with making decisions? Like, I'll sit there with my app open, and I just... I can't figure out if I should work on a class assignment, or pay a bill, or go start dinner. My brain just sort of stalls, and I end up sitting there doing none of it for a little while. 

I feel really silly even admitting that, because I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around being lazy! I really do want to get it all done. It's just hard to focus my thoughts sometimes to pick a starting point. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of example you were looking for.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has it been going on for weeks, months, or longer?

Um, well... I guess it's been a little while now. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know everyone gets tired and has off days! But, um, this stretch where I've been feeling so worn out and just... not really interested in doing much... I think it's been going on for about three months?

I mean, I've really been trying to push through it and keep up with everything, I promise. It's just been a bit quieter lately, and the fatigue is kind of heavy. But three months sounds about right, I think. Is that... is that a normal amount of time for something like this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or fidgety in a way that's unusual for you?

Um, well... I definitely don't think I'm restless or anything like that. I'm usually pretty calm, I think! 

But, um... I guess maybe on my slower days, I might be a little bit sluggish? I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I really do try my best to keep up. But sometimes it just feels like... like my body is moving through wet cement, if that makes sense? 

And, um, my spouse has pointed out that sometimes it takes me a weirdly long time just to answer a simple question. I feel so bad about it, because I don't want them to think I'm ignoring them! I really am listening. It just takes my brain a minute to put the words together and get them out. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too terrible. I really am trying to be more responsive. Is that the kind of thing you meant?
Have you ever felt so down or overwhelmed that you've thought about harming yourself or wished you weren't here?

Oh, um... no, no, definitely not! I mean, I know I've been a little tired and slow lately, but I would never... I really value my life, I promise. 

I mean, sure, sometimes when I'm feeling really overwhelmed with trying to get everything done, I might think, like, "Oh, I just want to crawl under the covers and sleep for a week." But that's just because I'm tired, you know? It's not because I don't want to be here. I really want to get better and get back to being helpful around the house and everything. 

I hope you don't think I'm... I don't know, unstable or anything just because I've been having a hard time. I really am trying my best to stay positive. Does that make sense? I just want to reassure you that I'm perfectly safe, really.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in most or all activities, even ones you used to really enjoy?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I've *completely* lost interest, because I really do still like those things in theory! I just... I guess lately I've sort of stopped caring as much about the things that usually make me feel like myself. 

Like, usually I'm really into sketching, or going out to gallery openings. And I always try to keep up with cooking nice meals, doing my yoga, or even just playing tennis with a friend. But lately, I just... I haven't really been doing any of it. 

I don't want you to think I'm just being lazy or giving up, though! I really do plan to get back to all of it soon, I promise. It's just been a little hard to find the spark for them right now. Is it... is it okay that I'm taking a little break from those things? I hope that doesn't make me sound too boring or anything.
Would you say that you’ve experienced a significant loss of interest or pleasure in almost all activities, even ones you used to really enjoy?

Um, I know we just talked about this a little bit, and I... I hope I'm explaining it right. I definitely haven't lost interest *completely*, because I still love those things! 

It's just, um... I guess I have sort of stopped caring as much about the things that usually make me feel like myself. Like my sketching, or going to gallery openings. And usually I'm really good about cooking nice meals, doing my yoga, or even playing tennis with a friend. But lately, it's just... I haven't really been doing any of it. 

I really am going to get back to all of it, though! I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing on purpose. It's just a little hard to find the energy for them right now. I hope that's an okay answer? I really am trying my best to stay active when I can.
Would you say that most days, for most of the day, you feel down or depressed, even when you're not physically tired?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I feel down *most* of the day. I mean, I definitely have moments where I feel a little low, but I try really hard not to let it take over, you know? 

I think a lot of it really is just feeling physically tired. When I don't have the energy to do things, it kind of makes me feel a bit disappointed in myself, but I wouldn't call it being depressed all day. I always try to put on a brave face and focus on the positives. 

I really don't want to sound like a complainer or someone who just wallows. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are, because I really am trying my best to stay upbeat.
Would you say that you feel down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day, even when you’re not feeling physically tired?

Um, I know we just touched on this, and I... I hope I'm not repeating myself too much or being frustrating. But, um, no, I really wouldn't say I feel depressed most of the day. 

Like I said, I definitely have some moments where I feel a bit flat, but I really try to push through it. I don't want to be someone who just sits around feeling sorry for themselves, you know? So I try to keep my chin up. 

I think when I do feel a little down, it's mostly just because I'm so worn out and I can't do the things I want to do. It's more frustration than depression, I think. I really hope I'm explaining this right... I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know. Is that helpful?
Have you found yourself struggling to think clearly, concentrate, or make decisions, nearly every day?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I'm struggling, exactly. I mean, I definitely try to stay organized! I even have this great planning app on my phone to help keep me on track. 

But, um, I guess lately I do have these moments where I get a little stuck? Like, I'll sit there with my app open, and I just can't seem to decide if I should work on a class assignment, or maybe pay a bill, or just start dinner. And then, because I don't want to make the wrong choice, I just kind of... end up not doing any of it for a little while. 

But I always figure it out eventually! I just get a little overwhelmed sometimes, I think. I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or scattered. I'm just trying to make sure I do things right, you know? Does that make sense?
Would you say that your interest in activities you used to enjoy has decreased to the point where they no longer bring you much pleasure or satisfaction at all?

Um, well... I wouldn't say they bring me *no* pleasure at all. I mean, I still think they're wonderful things to do! 

But, I guess... lately, I haven't really been keeping up with them as much as I usually do. Like, I usually love sketching, and going to gallery openings, or cooking a nice meal... even doing yoga or playing tennis with my friend. But recently, I just kind of... stopped doing them. 

It's not that I don't care about them anymore! I think I just haven't had the right mindset for it lately. I really hope that doesn't sound like I'm just giving up on my hobbies or being boring. I just haven't felt like myself enough to really get into them, if that makes sense? I'm definitely planning to get back to it soon, though! Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities, to the point where even things you used to really enjoy no longer feel meaningful or rewarding to you?

Um, I know we just talked about my hobbies, and I... I really don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm just being difficult. But I guess... if I'm being completely honest, it might be a little more than just not having the right mindset. 

I suppose I have kind of... stopped caring about the things that usually make me feel like myself. Like the sketching, the gallery openings, the cooking... even the yoga and playing tennis. It's like I know I *should* enjoy them, and I want to be the kind of person who does, but... they just haven't felt rewarding lately. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm ungrateful or just a negative person. I really try to find the good in things! It's just been a bit harder lately to feel that spark, I guess. I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question properly. Is that what you meant by losing interest?
Would you say that most days, for most of the day, you feel down or depressed, even when you're not physically tired?

Um, well... I definitely wouldn't say I feel down most of the day. I mean, I try really hard to keep a positive attitude! I think it's so important to focus on the bright side of things. 

I do have moments where I feel a little... flat, maybe? But I wouldn't call it depressed. I just think everyone has days where they aren't feeling one hundred percent, right? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm complaining or being dramatic. I'm generally a very cheerful person! 

I just haven't really noticed feeling sad all day long like that. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Would you say that you’ve experienced a complete loss of enjoyment or interest in nearly all activities, even ones you used to really look forward to, nearly every day?

Um, I know we've kind of gone over this a couple of times now, and I really don't want to seem like I'm just being difficult or, you know, overly negative. I try so hard to be upbeat! 

But... yes, I guess if I'm really looking at it honestly, it's pretty much every day right now. I just... I stopped caring about the things that usually make me feel like myself. The sketching, the gallery openings, cooking, yoga, even playing tennis with my friend... I just don't look forward to them at all anymore. 

I feel so bad admitting that, because I know how lucky I am to have hobbies and friends to do things with. I really hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or ungrateful. I want to enjoy them again, I really do! It's just been so hard to find that motivation lately. Does that... does that answer what you were asking? I hope I'm being helpful.
